name: Hidden Enemies
summary: Thrall sends you against the Searing Blade beneath Orgrimmar. You have won Neeru Fireblade's trust by pretending to share the cult's cause. Now Thrall sends you into Ragefire Chasm to strike at its leaders.

sections.title: A Cancer Beneath the Streets
sections.body: Orgrimmar was built as a haven for a free Orcish race. Yet beneath its markets, the Cleft of Shadow opens onto the tunnels of Ragefire Chasm. There, remnants of the Shadow Council gather strength as the Searing Blade. They practice dark arts and scheme to seize the young Horde from within its own capital.

sections.title: Playing the Double Agent
sections.body: A direct strike without knowledge would leave the Shadow Council's network intact. Thrall turns to you to learn from Neeru Fireblade, a warlock in the Cleft of Shadow who seems willing to cooperate. Neeru believes you share the cult's cause. So he reveals the names of its underground leaders: Bazzalan, a corrupt satyr, and Jergosh the Invoker, a warlock.

sections.title: Decapitating the Searing Blade
sections.body: Thrall sends you into Ragefire Chasm to kill Bazzalan and Jergosh. Their deaths throw the cultists into chaos, but Neeru cannot learn who carried them out. Thrall plans to keep the warlock under watch. With its leaders gone, the cult reels, and the Horde's young city gains precious breathing room.

faq.q: Who orders the hit in Hidden Enemies?
faq.answer: Warchief Thrall orders the attack from the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar. He trusts you with sensitive work to secure the city's underbelly.

faq.q: Why doesn't Thrall just execute Neeru Fireblade?
faq.answer: Thrall keeps Neeru alive and under watch. Knowing the traitor lets the Warchief's scouts follow the Shadow Council's communications and anticipate plots, while denying the cult room for a hidden replacement.

faq.q: Where are Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker located?
faq.answer: Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker lie deep within Ragefire Chasm, reached through the Cleft of Shadow in Orgrimmar. Jergosh commands the cultists from a volcanic ledge, while Bazzalan lurks in a nearby elevated cavern.

The Searing Blade is a local sect aligned with the Burning Blade and Shadow Council. Its members worship demonic powers and practice fel magic beneath Orgrimmar. They seek to overthrow Thrall and enslave the Horde again.

faq.q: Why is a satyr like Bazzalan working beneath an Orc city?
aliases: why is there a satyr in orgrimmar
faq.answer: Satyrs are ancient servants of the Burning Legion. Beneath the Orc city, Bazzalan acts as a demonic handler and instigator. He guides the Searing Blade's mortal cultists in carrying out the Legion's will under Thrall's feet.

faq.q: How does this quest fit into the broader Ragefire Chasm run?
faq.answer: Hidden Enemies brings Thrall's work to infiltrate the Searing Blade to its climax. It joins other Ragefire Chasm assignments against the place's chief humanoid foes in one coordinated strike.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you face demonic corruption in the heart of Durotar. It threatens all the new Horde fought to establish. Cleansing Ragefire Chasm helps preserve its hard-won freedom.
As an orc seeking redemption from the blood-haze, you face the Shadow Council's remnants beneath Orgrimmar. Their destruction is a matter of cultural survival and honor.
As a warlock, you know Thrall tolerates dark arts in the Horde's defense. Jergosh and the Searing Blade have sworn themselves to demonic masters and betrayed the Horde.
